messages.subject: Sampling a noisy ODE
parts:
Ultimately I want to infer a parameter in a hidden Markov model but for now I just want to generate some noisy data. I've adapted the example in Figure 19.2 of the Stan Reference Manual 2.9.0 to be a pendulum of unit length and mass so no longer linear.

functions {
  real[] pendulum(real t,
             real[] y,
             real[] theta,
             real[] x_r,
             int[] x_i) {
    real dydt[2];
    dydt[1] <- y[2];
    dydt[2] <- - theta[1] * sin(y[1]);
    return dydt;
  }
}
data {
  int<lower=1> T;
  real y0[2];
  real t0;
  real ts[T];
  // real theta[1];
  // real theta[2];
  real theta[3];
}
transformed data {
  real x_r[0];
  int x_i[0];
}
model {
}
generated quantities {
  real y_hat[T,2];
  y_hat <- integrate_ode(pendulum, y0, t0, ts, theta, x_r, x_i);
  // add measurement error
  for (t in 1:T) {
    y_hat[t,1] <- y_hat[t,1] + normal_rng(0,0.1);
    y_hat[t,2] <- y_hat[t,2] + normal_rng(0,0.1);
  }
}

And I am using this R to run the above.

library(rstan)

samples <- stan(file = 'Pendulum.stan',
                data = list (T  = 100,
                             y0 = c(1.6, 0.0),
                             t0 = 0.0,
                             ts = seq(0.1,10,0.1),
                             ## theta  = c(9.81)
                             ## theta  = c(9.81,9.81)
                             theta  = c(9.81,9.81,9.81)
                             ),
                algorithm="Fixed_param",
                chains = 1,
                iter =1
                )

s <- extract(samples,permuted=FALSE)
print(dimnames(s))
plot(s[1,1,1:100])

This works fine but if I change the Stan to be

  real theta[1];
  // real theta[2];
  // real theta[3];

and the R to be

                             theta  = c(9.81)
                             ## theta  = c(9.81,9.81)
                             ## theta  = c(9.81,9.81,9.81)

I get

Error : mismatch in number dimensions declared and found in context; processing stage=data initialization; variable name=theta; dims declared=(1); dims found=()
failed to create the sampler; sampling not done

I have two questions:

  1. What am I doing wrong to get this message?
  2. I think I only want one chain and one iteration to generate samples but maybe I have misunderstood how one should use Stan in this mode?
Many thanks, Dominic.

                             ## theta  = c(9.81)
                             ## theta  = c(9.81,9.81)
                             theta  = c(9.81,9.81,9.81)
                             ),
                algorithm="Fixed_param",

                iter =1
                )

print(dimnames(s))

This works fine but if I change the Stan to be

  real theta[1];
  // real theta[2];
  // real theta[3];

and the R to be

                             theta  = c(9.81)
                             ## theta  = c(9.81,9.81)
                             ## theta  = c(9.81,9.81,9.81)

I get

Error : mismatch in number dimensions declared and found in context; processing stage=data initialization; variable name=theta; dims declared=(1); dims found=()
failed to create the sampler; sampling not done

I have two questions:

  1. What am I doing wrong to get this message?

There is an ambiguity with R's 1-dimensional vectors. RStan passes that as Stan's real type. The fix from RStan is to explicitly construct it as an array, which will force the specified data to be compatible with a real array, vector, or row_vector. 
  theta = array(9.81, dims = 1)
1. I think I only want one chain and one iteration to generate samples but maybe I have misunderstood how one should use Stan in this mode?

No, no misunderstanding. 

Many thanks, Dominic.
